validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently FERC-regulated project, not a GEM-only entity. Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC (FGT) filed an application under NGA section 7(c) on 2024-12-13 in FERC Docket No. CP25-30-000 for its 'South Central Louisiana Project' (Federal Register notice 2025-00090, 2025-01-07, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/01/07/2025-00090/florida-gas-transmission-llc-notice-of-application-and-establishing-intervention-deadline -- verified live, names the project and docket verbatim). Independently, FGT's own landowner public notice (louisianapublicnotice.com, published 2024-12-22, https://louisianapublicnotice.com/notices/473064) and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (tracked across 7 releases, 2025-01 through 2026-08, docket CP25-30 in every release) corroborate the same project. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType='transmission' is correct -- this is an NGA section 7(c)-certificated addition to FGT's ~5,381-mile interstate natural gas transmission system (per FGT's own public notice), not a gathering/distribution line. Note: EIA's own 'Pipeline Type' field records this SPECIFIC project as 'Intrastate' with crosses_state_border='No' -- that field describes whether THIS discrete project's facilities cross a state line (they do not; both compressor stations are in Louisiana), not whether FGT's overall certificated system is interstate-class. It does not contradict GEM's transmission/gathering-axis classification. DUPLICATE: checked against the full FGT family on this gem.wiki page and the batch roster -- P3192 (FGT Big Bend, a separate Florida delivery-expansion project, already swept) is unrelated; the roster flags that P5548 'FGT South Louisiana' (batch A2, swept in parallel) carries a similarly-worded name but is stated to be a different project -- P7824 is specifically FERC Docket CP25-30 (CS 7.5 St. Landry Parish uprate + new unit at CS 8 East Baton Rouge Parish, 75,000 MMBtu/d to Tampa Electric), a discrete, docket-identified scope, so no duplicate finding here, but flagging the name-similarity risk for whoever reconciles P5548. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1/Operator = 'Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' (100%) matches both the FERC certificate applicant/holder and EIA's independently-compiled operator field -- correct, no relabeling needed. REF-QUALITY FINDING: every HAS_REF cell on this row (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Construction, Length, Location, Owner) carried the same current_ref, https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php#pipelines -- confirmed by direct fetch to be EIA's generic Natural Gas topic landing/navigation page (search, browse-by-topic, glossary links; no mention of Florida Gas Transmission or this project anywhere on the page). This is exactly the banned navigation-surface pattern (site root / data.php, never citable) and explains why the worklist's own existing_ref_checks flagged 'name not found' or 'value not found' on every one of these cells. All six are replaced below with article-class FERC/Federal Register and dated-EIA-release refs.

EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, which tracks this exact docket in every release from 2025-01 through 2026-08, shows the status field itself progressing: 'Applied' (2025-01 through 2026-01 releases) -> 'Approved' (2026-05 release, last_updated_date 2026-04-21, note: 'FERC approved 11/24/2025') -> 'Construction' (2026-08 release, last_updated_date 2026-07-06, notes still describe the same compression-only scope at CS 7.5/CS 8 with $43.4M cost and a 2027 in-service target). The Nov-23-2025 procedural deadline set by FERC itself and EIA's separately-tracked Nov-24-2025 approval date are one day apart, which is exactly the expected pattern for an order issued right at a self-set deadline -- two independently-sourced signals agreeing on timing even though I could not retrieve the order text itself (elibrary.ferc.gov serves a JS shell and its search API returns 403/406 to a scripted client; www.ferc.gov's commission-meeting-summary pages also 403). Recommend Status -> construction. StartYear1=2027 and ConstructionYear=2026 both remain correct and consistent with this progression, so no other status-linked date column changes. No staleness-rule dormancy applies (this is an affirmative forward progression from Applied through Approved to Construction, each release close on the heels of the last, not a stalled project).
